body:
## 3-Line TL;DR

- On standard API rates, GPT-6 Luna costs **$0.10/$0.50** per million input/output tokens, GPT-6 Sol **$2/$10** and Claude Opus 5.5 **$4/$20** ([OpenAI pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5/))
- A token price is not a task price: tokens per task, retries and review minutes decide the bill, and one Hacker News commenter reported that Luna's extra tokens erased its discount on their evals
- My impression is that Sol and Luna are excellent value while Opus 5.5 produces strong finished work, so I'd send checkable work to Luna first and call it a saving only after counting accepted tasks

## The price sheet, including the rows that don't make the keynote

| Standard API, per 1m tokens | Input | Cached input | Output | 1m in + 250k out |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPT-6 Luna | $0.10 | $0.01 | $0.50 | **$0.225** |
| GPT-6 Sol | $2 | $0.20 | $10 | **$4.50** |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | $4 | $0.20 | $20 | **$9.00** |

*Sources: [OpenAI API pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) — Standard, short-context tier; [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5/) — Opus 5.5 pricing table. Checked 2026-09-27*

![Input and output API token rates for GPT-6 Luna, Sol, and Claude Opus 5.5](/images/posts/agi/gpt-6-api-prices.webp)

- The last column is our arithmetic across many requests: `input / 1m × input rate + output / 1m × output rate`. It is not a task size, and not a claim that one request holds that much
- Cached input is where the headline gets awkward. Sol and Opus 5.5 both charge **$0.20** per million cached tokens, and Anthropic says cache reads make up the majority of agentic and coding costs ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5/)). If that describes your agent loop, "half the price of Opus" applies to the smaller lines of the bill
- The fine print moves the numbers both ways: OpenAI's long-context tier raises Sol to $4/$15 and Luna to $0.20/$0.75, Batch and Flex halve the standard rates ([OpenAI pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing)), and Opus 5.5 Fast mode costs $8/$40 ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5/))

## Both vendors now sell per-task savings. Read who measured them

- Anthropic says Opus 5.5 at default settings costs 40% less than Opus 5 on typical workloads in its tests, because the rates fell and it uses fewer tokens per task ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5/)). That is the maker's workload, not your repository
- OpenAI's price list shows GPT-5.6 Sol at $4/$20 and GPT-5.6 Luna at $0.20/$1.20 ([OpenAI pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing)). Against GPT-6, input halves for both, and Luna's output rate drops 58%
- A rate cut becomes a task-cost cut only if tokens per task stay flat. Half the rate with twice the thinking is the same bill with a better press release
- So the unit worth tracking is dollars per accepted task, measured on your own work. Everything else is a coupon

## Give the cheap model a job with an actual finish line

- The table below is an **operating proposal** built from price and how easily a result can be checked. It is not a ranking from a controlled three-model experiment

| Work | Try first | Acceptance check | Escalate when |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Classification, fixed-field extraction | Luna | Required fields present, value traceable to the source, label from the allowed list | Fields go missing or values have no source |
| Small, bounded code changes | Luna or Sol | Relevant tests pass, requirement met, diff stays in scope | Tests pass but the requirement quietly didn't make it |
| Design, long or subtle writing | Include Opus 5.5 | Human review of logic, omissions and factual support | The prose is more confident than its evidence |

- Valid JSON proves the brackets behaved. It says nothing about whether a plausible value was invented to fill a blank, so compare extracted values with the original
- My preference for Opus 5.5 is about the finished output I have seen. It is not a measured success rate, and I won't stretch it into "better at every task"

![Acceptance checks, bounded retries, and escalation; all costs stay with the task](/images/posts/ai/acceptance-pipeline.webp)

## Count the failures, or every model wins

1. Pick recurring tasks and fix the inputs, acceptance check, tools and retry limit before the first run. Lowering the bar after each failure is a very efficient way to win your own benchmark
2. Log attempts, accepted tasks, total API spend including failed calls, retries and review minutes for each model
3. Compute **API cost per accepted task = total API spend ÷ accepted tasks**. Zero accepted tasks is a failure, not a very low unit cost
4. Keep review minutes in their own column. Turning them into dollars needs one hourly rate for everyone; adding minutes to dollars directly just produces a confident wrong number
5. When a task hits the retry limit, escalate it and charge the escalation to the original task, not to the stronger model's budget

## Community Reactions

- A commenter running internal cybersecurity evals found GPT-6 Luna used far more tokens than GPT-5.6 Luna for the same result at a given thinking effort, and took longer; the extra tokens wiped out the 50% saving for them ([Hacker News](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49856057))
- Another developer ran 36 agent-and-tool scenarios from their app: GPT-6 Luna passed 30, GPT-5.6 Luna 33. The suite was tuned for 5.6, and they kept 5.6 as the default ([Hacker News](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49814239))
- On the other side, one user has Astra plan, Luna write code and Sol review it and run integration tests, and reports about 20% better usage efficiency and 20% faster completion. Their setup, their numbers ([Hacker News](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49806361))
- In the Opus 5.5 thread, a commenter pointed out that Artificial Analysis's cost to run its intelligence index came out higher than for the previous Opus ([Hacker News](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49805082)). A vendor's typical workload and a third-party index are different jobs, which is rather the point

## Q&A (Field Notes)

- **Q: Luna is the cheapest. Should everything go there?**
  - Start with work that has an automatic check, and track tokens per accepted task. A lower rate can hide more tokens, more retries or omissions you only find later
- **Q: Is Sol really half the price of Opus 5.5?**
  - On standard input and output rates, yes. On cached input both charge $0.20, and the reasoning effort you choose changes tokens per task
- **Q: Does Batch pricing change the answer?**
  - For work that can wait, OpenAI's Batch tier halves the rates. It does not change acceptance rates or review minutes
- **Q: Does Opus 5.5 always write better?**
  - Not established here. My impression concerns finished output; run the same drafts against the same acceptance check before deciding
- **Q: Can these prices compare ChatGPT or Claude subscriptions?**
  - No. API billing and subscription usage limits are separate systems
title: GPT-6 Luna and Sol vs Opus 5.5: The Token Price Isn’t the Task Price
description: Luna and Sol undercut Opus 5.5 on token rates, but cached input, retries and tokens per task decide the bill: official prices, fine print and a cost-per-accepted-task check
imageAlt: Notebook comparing USD output token rates with retry and review costs
